title: Add tokenizer smoke-checks and template delimiter normalizer during onboarding
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: When we onboard new open models we sometimes see subtle tokenizer-chat-template mismatches (role delimiter variants, invisible control chars, subtoken boundary shifts) that cause prompt truncation, unexpected token counts, or failed structured parsing. These issues propagate into incorrect performance profiles and lead to poor model pin recommendations. Goal: implement a lightweight compatibility layer in the onboarding pipeline that runs tokenizer smoke-checks, normalizes common delimiter and whitespace variants for chat templates, emits deterministic warnings/errors, and optionally auto-fixes non-destructive cases. This should reduce onboarding churn, improve perf-profile accuracy, and make pinning decisions safer.
acceptance_criteria: Add a tokenizer smoke-check job in onboarding that validates: round-trip decode stability for representative prompts, consistent role delimiter tokenization, and determinism of special tokens (e.g., <|assistant|>, <|system|>)
Implement a configurable normalization pass that canonicalizes common role delimiter patterns and removes zero-width/invisible chars without altering user-visible content
Onboarding UI/CI shows structured warnings for models that fail checks and blocks publishing perf profiles unless a reviewer marks the failure as reviewed
Provide an 'auto-fix' mode that suggests a normalized template and a one-click accept in the Console; auto-fix is off by default and must be enabled per-model
Add metrics and dashboard: percentage of onboarded models with tokenizer/template mismatches, mean token-count delta before/after normalization, and number of pinned models updated due to fix
Document rules and caveats in the onboarding Confluence page and link to the normalization heuristics in the PR
implementation_steps: Add new onboarding job 'tokenizer-compatibility-check' in model-onboard pipeline (Kubernetes job triggered post-index).
Create a lightweight test corpus of representative chat prompts and structured outputs used to exercise role delimiters and special tokens.
Implement normalization library in infra-lang: functions to canonicalize known delimiter variants, strip zero-width spaces, and record token-index mappings for traceability.
Expose checks as pass/warn/fail with machine-readable reasons; wire results into the onboarding state machine and Console UI.
Add a feature-flagged auto-fix code path that produces a suggested normalized template and Git-style diff shown in Console.
Add e2e tests and unit tests for all normalization rules and smoke-check heuristics; include cases from previous incidents (see comments).
Publish perf-profile only when reviewer-approved or when the model passes checks; otherwise publish with a 'compatibility-untested' tag and gated pin recommendations.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): Enable job on 10% of onboarding runs behind feature flag; emit warnings but do not block publishing (2 weeks).
Phase 2 (Enforced Warnings): Enable for 50% of runs; surface warnings prominently in Console and require explicit reviewer acknowledgement before perf-profile publication (2 weeks).
Phase 3 (Enforced Blocking): Default enable for all onboarding runs; optionally allow bypass via explicit 'accept risk' flow for SRE/ModelOps (after monitoring metrics for 2 weeks).
Monitor: token-count-delta, false-positive rate (developer overrides), time-to-onboard, and customer-facing incidents. Roll back normalization rules if false-positive > 8% over 7d.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: Do not mutate user-provided prompts at serving time. Normalization is applied only to onboarding templates and suggested to users as an explicit change; rationale: avoid runtime surprises and preserve user intent.
Trade-off: Conservative normalization rules to minimize false positives mean some odd cases will remain flagged for manual review. We accept a small manual burden to avoid breaking edge semantics.
Decision: Auto-fix behind opt-in flag only. Immediate auto-fix could hide subtle semantic changes in templates that affect generation; require explicit consent in Console.
Trade-off: Adding checks increases onboarding latency by ~1-2s on average for CPU-bound tokenization tests; acceptable given reduced downstream regressions.
